task.title: Contributors
task.shortdesc: Funds brought in by promoters and owners of the business are called equity capital. Equity

context.p: Funds brought in by promoters and owners of the business are called equity capital. Equity capital can be brought in at the start of a business or at a later date as the business grows. Equity capital also can be contributed by outside investors. To enable such contribution, the business offers equity shares to outside investors, who become shareholders.

Funds brought in as loan is called debt capital. Those that contribute debt capital are called lenders to the business. Lenders can be individuals or institutions including banks. To enable such lending, a business issues debt instruments to investors, or obtains term loans by mortgaging the assets of the company.
